definitions.explanation: The condition of something becoming old and deteriorated through age and wear. Primarily used for buildings, infrastructure, and equipment — not for living things.

examples.japanese: {老朽|ろうきゅう}した{建物|たてもの}を{取|と}り{壊|こわ}す。
インフラの{老朽|ろうきゅう}{化|か}が{深刻|しんこく}な{問題|もんだい}になっている。
examples.english: The deterioration of infrastructure is becoming a serious problem.

examples.japanese: {老朽|ろうきゅう}{化|か}した{水道管|すいどうかん}の{交換|こうかん}{工事|こうじ}には{莫大|ばくだい}な{費用|ひよう}がかかるため、{自治体|じちたい}の{財政|ざいせい}を{圧迫|あっぱく}している。
examples.english: Replacing deteriorated water pipes requires enormous costs, putting pressure on municipal finances.

notes:
USAGE NOTE:
Almost always used with {化|か} (= becoming ~) as {老朽|ろうきゅう}{化|か}. Applied to physical structures and equipment, not to people. A common topic in Japanese news, particularly regarding aging infrastructure.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {老朽|ろうきゅう}{化|か} (aging, deterioration)
- {老朽|ろうきゅう}{化|か}した (deteriorated, dilapidated)
- {老朽|ろうきゅう}{化|か}が{進|すす}む (deterioration advances)
- {老朽|ろうきゅう}{化|か}{対策|たいさく} (measures against deterioration)
- {老朽|ろうきゅう}{施設|しせつ} (aging facilities)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {劣化|れっか}: degradation, deterioration (broader; can apply to quality, materials, or data)
- {荒廃|こうはい}: ruin, devastation (implies more severe decay or abandonment)
